skill.name: set-up-shopware-meta-returning-customer-bidding
skill.description: Use Product Metrics to check Shopware repeat-order tracking and guide returning customer bidding in Meta. Verify a test event before choosing a revenue or profit conversion in Meta.
skill.summary: Verify paid Shopware repeat-order events and set up a returning customer conversion in Meta.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most alerts matched Markdown formatting, documentation links, or routine setup steps. Confirmed risks include an unpinned installer, authenticated writes, sensitive order reads, and remote tool access. The review also found unsafe token handling, broader tracking than the task suggests, and conflicting profit event instructions.

remediation.issue: The instructions tell the assistant to collect and pass the Meta access token to a command.
remediation.suggestion: Require direct token entry in the verified Product Metrics app. Remove every instruction that sends a token through chat or command arguments.

remediation.issue: The installer does not pin the package version or repository revision.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the installer package and reviewed skill revision. Require approval before running the installer or installing the Shopware extension.

remediation.issue: The workflow allows authenticated writes and broad tracking setup without requiring explicit approval of the data scope.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the company, property, sales channel, Meta dataset, and event categories before a write. Explain what enabling delivery shares and verify consent first.

remediation.issue: Order checks can retrieve individual order margins when classification is all the user requested.
remediation.suggestion: Use a classification-only query or return aggregate counts. Require explicit approval before retrieving or displaying order-level financial details.

remediation.issue: The main workflow and the returning customer guide disagree on the profit event.
remediation.suggestion: Use the returning customer profit event and its purpose rule consistently. Test that first orders do not match the conversion before changing campaign optimization.

remediation.issue: The Shopware guide describes tracking from a random storefront path as resistant to ad blocking.
remediation.suggestion: Remove routing intended to defeat blocking. Document how storefront tracking respects shopper consent and browser privacy controls.

semantic_findings.title: Assistant Is Told to Collect a Meta Access Token
semantic_findings.description: The Meta guide says to enter the token in the app but also says the assistant must ask for it. Passing the token to a command can expose it in tool records or process arguments.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both files explicitly allow assistant handling of the token. No evidence found of an actual disclosure or of a protected secret input.

semantic_findings.title: Setup Can Enable Tracking Beyond Repeat Orders
semantic_findings.description: The prerequisite enables Meta delivery when tracking is not live, without a separate event scope approval step. The destination can send checkout events, purchased products, and customer matching data in addition to repeat-order conversions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guide leaves sending enabled and lists broader data categories. It documents shopper consent, so this is a setup scope risk, not evidence of unauthorized transfer.

semantic_findings.title: Profit Setup Can Optimize for the Wrong Orders
semantic_findings.description: The main instructions point to the general order profit event. Following them can make a retention campaign optimize for first orders as well as repeat orders.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The main workflow names the general profit event, while the repeat-order guide names a different profit event and purpose rule.

semantic_findings.title: Tracking Script Is Designed to Resist Ad Blocking
semantic_findings.description: The Shopware guide describes a tracking script served from a random storefront path and links to an ad-blocker-proof feature. This design can reduce the effectiveness of browser blocking independently of consent settings.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guide connects the random path to a feature labeled ad-blocker-proof. No evidence found that it overrides the configured consent banner.

content.user_title: Set Up Shopware Returning Customer Bidding in Meta
content.value_statement: A Meta retention campaign needs to distinguish paid repeat orders from first purchases. Use Product Metrics to verify the repeat-order event and configure a conversion that uses its revenue or profit.
actual_capabilities: Read Product Metrics setup status to see whether the Shopware sales channel and Meta destination are connected.
Guide an administrator through pairing one Shopware sales channel with Product Metrics.
Check whether recent paid orders were classified as new, returning, or unknown.
Guide a test of repeat-order event delivery in Meta Events Manager.
Explain how to create a custom conversion and choose it as the ad set's optimization event.
limitations: The connection requires compatible Shopware 6.7, PHP 8.2 or later, and a Product Metrics Pro workspace.
Each installation uses paid order history from one sales channel only.
Profit events need complete cost data. Historical orders are not imported, and later refunds do not revise Meta events.
The merchant creates the custom conversion and selects the campaign event in Meta.

use_cases.title: Check Store Readiness
use_cases.description: Find out whether your Shopware sales channel is paired and what remains before you can test a returning customer conversion.

use_cases.title: Configure a Retention Conversion
use_cases.description: Use a verified repeat-order event to create a custom conversion for a retention ad set.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Missing Repeat-Order Events
use_cases.description: Check payment status, channel scope, and consent to explain why a repeat purchase did not appear in Meta.

prompt_templates.title: Check Setup Readiness
prompt_templates.scenario: You have not set up bidding for returning customers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether my Shopware sales channel and Meta destination are connected in Product Metrics. List missing steps without changing any settings.

prompt_templates.title: Review Order Classifications
prompt_templates.scenario: Tracking is connected and you want to check classifications.
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize how Product Metrics classified my last 20 paid Shopware orders in the selected sales channel. Report counts only and omit customer details and margins.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Repeat-Order Test
prompt_templates.scenario: Your repeat-order event is not visible in Events Manager.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to test a paid repeat order with marketing and analytics consent. Explain what to verify in Events Manager before removing the test code.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Profit Conversion
prompt_templates.scenario: You want to optimize one retention ad set using repeat-order profit.
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify that my planned Meta conversion uses the returning customer profit event and its matching purpose rule. Check cost readiness and list the manual steps without changing my ad set.

output_examples.input: Is my Shopware sales channel ready to test repeat orders in Meta?
output_examples.output: The sales channel is active in Product Metrics, but the Meta destination is not connected. Add it in the Product Metrics app and enter the access token there, not in chat.

output_examples.input: Why was my test order classified as new when this guest has ordered before?
output_examples.output: The prior paid order was in another sales channel. Repeat the test in the same sales channel with a guest email that already has a paid order there.

output_examples.input: I can see the returning customer revenue event in Test events. What should I check next?
output_examples.output: Create a custom conversion that matches the returning customer revenue event and its purpose rule. Use the event value and currency, then confirm the next eligible repeat order registers after you remove the test code.

best_practices: Verify the sales channel, Product Metrics property, and Meta dataset before enabling delivery.
Enter the Meta access token in the Product Metrics app and the pairing token in Shopware Administration.
Verify a repeat order with marketing and analytics consent before selecting its conversion in one retention ad set.
anti_patterns: Choosing the general order profit conversion for an ad set that should optimize only for returning customers.
Expecting a purchase in a different sales channel to establish repeat customer status.
Leaving the Meta test event code enabled while expecting events to appear in live reporting.

faq.question: What counts as a returning customer?
faq.answer: The customer must have an earlier paid order in the same sales channel. Product Metrics matches by Shopware customer account or guest email.

faq.question: Can I use Shopware 5?
faq.answer: No. The documented plugin supports Shopware 6.7 and requires PHP 8.2 or later.

faq.question: Why is the returning customer event missing from Meta?
faq.answer: Meta lists the event only after it receives one. Check that the repeat order was paid and that the shopper gave marketing and analytics consent.

faq.question: When can I use the returning customer profit event?
faq.answer: Use it when additional costs are enabled and the order has complete cost data. A loss-making order is sent with a conversion value of zero.

faq.question: What customer data goes to Meta?
faq.answer: With marketing consent, Advanced Matching sends hashed email, name, postal code, and country, plus IP address and browser information. Browser IDs also require ad storage consent.

faq.question: Will old orders and later refunds change the conversion data?
faq.answer: No. Product Metrics does not import past orders into Meta, and later refunds do not revise events already sent.
